name: Breathing Scaffold
subtitle: an organ frame that supplies its own oxygen

effects.effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
gases spread out on their own from crowded to empty

effect: sponge-like crystals with a huge inner surface trap one chosen gas
how: Lab-grown tissue thicker than a few millimetres dies in the middle, because oxygen cannot reach it before blood vessels grow in. The scaffold the cells grow on is laced with crystal sponges loaded with oxygen, which seeps out slowly to the surrounding cells for the week or two the vessels need to form.
obstacle: The sponges hold only a few days of oxygen and must break down safely once empty.
why: Oxygen-releasing scaffolds use peroxides today; crystal-sponge oxygen stores are untested.
real: Reviews list MOFs among emerging oxygen sources for thick engineered tissue, but demonstrated oxygen-releasing scaffolds use calcium peroxide or perfluorocarbons; no MOF oxygen-loaded scaffold was found.
